s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute neurological deterioration with impaired extraocular movement, tetraparesis, and signs of meningeal irritation
salient_findings: Mild sinking of the right leg
key_facts: 10-year history of treatment with various medications
No history of severe lymphocytopenia
Impaired extraocular movement at last outpatient visit
Mild sinking of the right leg at position test
Developed dizziness and nausea a few months later
Received methylprednisolone treatment
Presented with moderate tetraparesis, headache, fever, and neck stiffness
Family members had fever, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, recovering within 3 days
Patient had mild gastrointestinal symptoms prior to neurological symptoms
Positive Romberg test
Initial white blood cell count: 4900/μL
Lymphocyte count: 1240/μL
Later white blood cell count: 18,000/μL
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed increased protein level and 108 cells/mL
Cerebrospinal fluid culture was positive
MRI showed hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum with slight contrast enhancement

shortlist.label: Cryptococcal Meningitis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive cerebrospinal fluid culture and signs of meningeal irritation

shortlist.label: Tuberculous Meningitis
shortlist.why_kept: Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed increased protein level and 108 cells/mL, consistent with chronic infection

shortlist.label: Listeria Meningitis
shortlist.why_kept: Impaired extraocular movement, mild sinking of the right leg, and positive Romberg test suggest brainstem involvement

shortlist.label: Brainstem Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: MRI showed hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum with slight contrast enhancement

shortlist.label: CNS Vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute neurological deterioration with impaired extraocular movement, tetraparesis, and signs of meningeal irritation

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, such as impaired extraocular movement, mild sinking of the right leg, dizziness, nausea, and neck stiffness, along with the cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing increased protein level and 108 cells/mL with 95% neutrophils, are consistent with Listeria Meningitis. The patient's recent history of mild gastrointestinal symptoms and the family members' similar symptoms also support this diagnosis, as Listeria is often associated with foodborne outbreaks.

rejected.label: Cryptococcal Meningitis
rejected.why: Typically associated with severe lymphocytopenia, which the patient does not have.

rejected.label: Tuberculous Meningitis
rejected.why: Usually presents with a more chronic course and does not typically cause acute gastrointestinal symptoms in family members.

rejected.label: Brainstem Encephalitis
rejected.why: Does not fully explain the cerebrospinal fluid findings and the patient's gastrointestinal symptoms.

rejected.label: CNS Vasculitis
rejected.why: Would not typically cause a positive cerebrospinal fluid culture.
